current.title: Super Shoes Just Broke The Marathon World Record Again
current.hook: Your shoes just broke the marathon record: 2 hours flat, and it's still falling.
current.closing: Somewhere, a shoe lab just shaved a few more seconds off human limits.
current.question: Should carbon-plated super shoes even count toward a world record? Tell me what you think.

segments.say: The men's marathon world record dropped from 2 hours 6 minutes in 1998 to 2 hours flat by 2023.

segments.topic: marathon world record improvement rate super shoes
segments.say: Before carbon-plated super shoes, the record fell about 8 seconds a year. Since 2016, it's almost 30 seconds a year.

segments.topic: marathon world record fastest times since super shoes
segments.say: Of the 20 fastest marathons ever run, 15 of them happened after 2018 -- right when the shoes arrived.

problems: seg2: both bubbles read 8.3 with the same 'Before 2016 (1988-2013)' label, and the kicker says 'BEFORE 2016 TOPS THE LIST', which is the opposite of the story.
seg1: the gauge counts up to an unlabelled '126' (minutes?) tagged 1998, so a falling record looks like a rising number.
Hook/seg0: a slow band creeping down a thin table. The '2 hours flat' moment never lands, and the table's last value is 120.6, not 120.
The mascot stands on top of bubbles or leans beside the scale and never causes the motion.
The CTA 'COMMENT BELOW' overprints the 'think.' line, and Data covers the 'Set since 2018' label.
Large empty dark areas in seg0 and seg3.
fixes: Fix the seg2 data join so the post-2016 value (~30 s/yr) and its label render, then show the rates as something that moves at those speeds, such as two clocks shaving seconds.
Show the record time as a runner or finish clock that Data pushes down from 2:06 to 2:00 in mm:ss, not raw '126'.
Put Data in the act: lacing a super shoe that carries the runner faster, or loading the 15 blocks onto the scale himself.
Move 'COMMENT BELOW' clear of the CTA text, and keep Data off the labels.
Make the hook open on the 2:00:35 clock smashing through the 2:00 line, not a slow fill.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'.
